Akeneo argues that while the first AI agent may solve a relatively straightforward use case, the challenge changes fundamentally as organisations deploy more of them. As the whitepaper states, “Your first agent is a use case. Your tenth is an operating model.” The paper identifies ten potential agents spanning the product lifecycle, including product modelling, supplier data, enrichment, content creation, localisation, asset intelligence, quality and compliance, activation, market intelligence, and insights. While individual AI agents are likely to become widely available, Akeneo argues this accessibility to the technology itself will therefore provide relatively little competitive differentiation. What will matter is whether agents can share trusted data, business rules, workflows, and governance. The warning comes as retailers and brands increasingly explore agentic AI to automate activities that have traditionally required significant manual intervention. Rather than relying on a single general-purpose AI assistant, Akeneo expects product teams will increasingly work alongside fleets of specialised agents, each responsible for different elements of managing, enriching and distributing product information. In June, the U.S. Food & Drug Administration approved its first new sunscreen filter in 25 years: bemotrizinol, or BEMT, an ingredient that’s been widely available in Europe and Asia since 2000 and 2002, respectively. The filter has been heralded online for its remarkably lightweight, smooth feel; larger molecule size; and ability to protect against both UVA, the rays that age skin, and UVB, the rays that burn skin. “We love that we now get a new tool, and it’s not just a flash in the pan because it’s the new thing on the block,” Brian Bodnar, L’Oréal Group principal scientist of photoprotection, North America, told Glossy. “It’s important that we protect against both UVA and UVB, which is a little bit more difficult when you don’t have a large UV filter toolset to use as we might have in other countries.” BEMT offers wider photo protection than U.S. filters like avobenzone or homosalate. “We [have] really lacked this middle ground [in the U.S.], right in between UVA and UVB,” he said. “It’s a wavelength area known as UVA 2, a short wavelength right in between, and BEMT helps us fill in the gap.” What’s more, BEMT is made from a larger molecule than other chemical filters available in the U.S., which means less of the formula soaks into the bloodstream, a mounting concern among some consumers who avoid endocrine disruptors or are prone to irritation from sunscreen. “It really doesn’t go into the skin almost at all in most formulations, so you don’t have to worry about that too much,” Bodnar said. articles.excerpt: It looks like we’ve only just spotted this (or rather thanks to a ChannelX reader!) – Royal Mail Live Tracking is live and if you’re expecting a parcel you may now be able to see how many stops away the postie is and as the item gets closer to you the delivery window could be narrowed to as little as fifteen or even ten minutes. We’re loving this last mile tracking – it’s standard for most couriers these days but we’ve not spotted it with Royal Mail before. You may already have seen it if you were in one of the early delivery areas for it to be rolled out and it’s a massive improvement on the two or more hours delivery windows you’ll be accustomed to from Royal Mail. One of the problems for Royal Mail which other carriers don’t face is mixed delivery routes where parcels and letters are on the same route. When you’re only tracking parcel delivery windows, how do you know how many houses have letters to be dropped off? This was a problem that was solved with expertise from Bettermile who have built the Royal Mail Live Tracking solution. Results show that consumers love this new feature and often parcel tracking will be refreshed up to nine times on the day of delivery. In half of cases the delivery window can be narrowed to less than 15 minutes and in a quarter of cases it’s a delivery slot of under 10 minutes which is about as good as it gets with any carrier. If it’s available for your delivery, you’ll see the tracking available on the Royal Mail website and we’d say give it a try!

articles.excerpt: Ahead of the holiday shopping season, eBay is introducing a new camera-first listing experience, with AI working behind the scenes to help sellers move from photos to a ready-to-review listing with less manual work. Sellers start by taking photos of an item, and eBay helps identify it and pre-fill the listing details. Sellers review the draft, make any changes and decide when to publish, making it easier to list items they no longer need, whether they’re looking to clear out space or earn extra cash for holiday shopping. By shifting the work from setup to review, eBay’s new listing experience eliminates manual data entry and takes the guesswork out of selling. While AI powers the creation, you remain completely in control. Nothing goes live without your approval: you can easily review the pre-filled information, make any edits, and decide exactly when your item is ready to list. More than 10 million unique sellers have used eBay’s AI features to date, and more than 800,000 new listings are being created every day with AI. The update builds on the simplified mobile listing experience eBay introduced last year. It does more of the setup for sellers while keeping them in control of the final listing.
